newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI allows bridge loans against shares.
newsitem.headline: India RBI allows bridge loans against shares.

text.p: Indian companies can take bridge loans against shares as they wait for capital to be raised through a public issue, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Tuesday.

"It has been decided to allow banks to extend loans to corporates against shares held by them to enable such corporates to meet the promoters' contribution to the equity of new companies in anticipation of raising resources," RBI Governor C. Rangarajan said in a statement to chief executives of banks.

Such loans will be treated as banks' investment in shares and would thus come under the five percent ceiling, he said in a statement spelling out the credit policy for the first six months of 1997/98 (April-March).
The margin and repayment schedule of the loans will be determined by the banks, the statement said.
